SCOTUS is not a trier of facts. Which means, it is beyond its function to make its own findings of certain vital facts different from those from a trial. When material facts are controverted they are issues that are usually litigated before a lower court. SCOTUS operates in an appellate jurisdiction and for emergency relief in matters of national security - of which a presidential election would qualify. A lower court is the jurisdiction to where the merits of a particular case, such as voter fraud, would be brought. They receive all the evidence to be presented by the parties, and only then come to a definite decision based on the merits of the evidence.
